svg.title: Seven
svg.desc:
The Seven's logo script, traced from the outline artwork 14 Nov 2026.
THE BOX BOTTOM IS THE LETTERS' BASELINE, and that is the whole point of this file's geometry. The traced ink runs to y=677; the viewBox stops at 626, which is where the feet of "even" sit. The S's descending tail occupies y 626-677 and paints OUTSIDE the box, which is what overflow="visible" is for.
Why it is cut here. The top tabs of the four-tab nav align on BASELINES, not boxes (the six changes locked 14 Nov 2026, change 2): a script face has a far deeper descender than a grotesque, so aligning boxes floats the word above the line its neighbours sit on. Daniel, 14 Nov: "The script's S has a long tail; dropping that tail on the rule shoves 'even' up above the words."
Baseline-aligned, an inline-block's own baseline IS its bottom margin edge. With the box cut at the baseline, the letters therefore land on the shared text baseline with no CSS offset anywhere — so every future use inherits the alignment from the artwork instead of re-deriving it. Do NOT nudge this with a margin or a relative top at the call site; that was the bug.
MEASURED, not eyeballed (rasterised and read row by row in the real renderer): the lettering stops at y=626, the tail reaches y=677, so the descender is 51 of 688 units = 7.41% of the traced box. At the 31px height the design was approved at, that is 2.30px of lift — which is exactly how far the letters were sitting above "Patches".
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HEIGHT. A consumer's `height` now scales 626 units, not 688, so the same number renders ~9.8% larger. 28.2px here is the 31px the design was checked at (31 x 626/688). Verified in a real window against "Patches" — which has no descenders, so the bottom of its ink IS the text baseline — at 0.00px in both themes and both states.
